question.text: A particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mi>M</mi></math> at rest disintegrates into two particles of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>M</mi></math>, respectively, having non zero velocities. The ratio of de-Broglie wavelength of particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>M</mi></math> to that of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>M</mi></math> will be:

solution.text:
λ=hp

Both the particles will move with momentum same in magnitude and opposite in direction.

So de Broglie wavelength of both will be same, i.e., ratio 1:1.
